column3: The Hebrew says the waters came up to the soul; BSB renders this up to my neck.
The Hebrew says I came into deep waters and the flood swept me away; BSB says I drifted into them and uses present engulfs.

The Hebrew calls those destroying him strong; BSB says many.
The Hebrew has guilts in the plural; BSB has guilt.

The Hebrew calls him a proverb or byword to them; BSB says he was sport to them.
The Hebrew says gate-sitters speak about him and names drinkers of strong drink; BSB says they mock him and calls the drinkers drunkards.

The Hebrew uses a passive plea, let me be rescued, in the second clause; BSB gives an active command, deliver me.
